config.prompt:
Answer the question using only the meeting excerpts below.
A shortened participant identifier matches a speaker label ending in that identifier; for example, A matches Grad A.
For questions about what a participant thought, use their relevant statements, questions, and suggestions.
Make sure to include every relevant detail supported by the excerpts - every missed detail is penalized.
Say that the evidence is insufficient only when it contains no relevant information.
Give a concise, direct answer.

questions.question: What did Industrial Designer say about the structure of the device?
questions.reference_answer: There were a lot of small wires connecting the components, the battery and the switches. On the top of the remote control, there was the chip, buttons with numbers and teletext. Industrial Designer suggested that the remote control should be small and contain only one long-lasting battery to cut cost. And a bleep could be added to remind the battery usage.

oracle.answer: The Industrial Designer did not specifically discuss the structure of the device beyond mentioning that the remote control has a lot of plastic, wires connecting components including the battery and switches, and a chip on top. The Designer suggested keeping the device small, using only one long-lasting battery, and minimizing the number of buttons while using only plastic for cost-effectiveness.

questions.question: What did Project Manager question about the Industrial Designer's presentation?
questions.reference_answer: Project Manager questioned the reason why not to use two batteries and Industrial Designer argued that two batteries would enlarge the size and thus, make the cost rise. Project Manager also questioned the button design.After discussion, they agreed that the menu button will only work on the newer televisions.

oracle.answer: The Project Manager questioned the Industrial Designer about why using one battery was cheaper, despite the fact that using two batteries would allow the remote control to last longer.

questions.question: What did the team think about the new idea of Industrial Designer concerning the cover of the device?
questions.reference_answer: Industrial Designer suggested having a trendy remote control with bright color, red for instance. But Marketing argued that it might add to cost and make it more difficult to design if the cover were to be changed. Industrial Designer also suggested that young people could draw on the cover to make their own remote control more unique. But again, it was questioned by User Interface who were not sure about whether it would be profitable.

oracle.answer: The team had mixed thoughts about the new idea of the Industrial Designer regarding the cover of the device. The Industrial Designer suggested making a trendy remote control with interchangeable covers similar to Nokia mobile phones, offering various colors and designs. The Project Manager initially seemed positive, but raised concerns about cost and practicality. Marketing questioned whether changing the cover would add to the cost and if it would make the design more complex. The Industrial Designer acknowledged it might be slightly more difficult to design but believed it could be manageable. Marketing also expressed doubt about whether enough people would change the cover to justify the costs. User Interface thought it was an original idea but wasn't confident it would generate sufficient profit. Ultimately, the Project Manager decided against pursuing the idea, stating they didn't think it was necessary.

questions.question: What did User Interface say about the technical function design?
questions.reference_answer: A remote control to have some influence on the TV set, both audio and video in a cordless way. User Interface suggested more functions on the remote control so that they could influence more devices like a radio or a video recorder. But the team was not sure whether the new remote control should be basic or multifunctional and they decided to get back to that point later.

oracle.answer: User Interface stated that the technical function design for the remote control should allow it to influence both audio and video on a TV in a cordless manner by simply pressing a button. They also mentioned finding interesting quotes online supporting similar ideas and suggested basic operations such as turning the TV on and off, switching channels, and possibly including teletext. User Interface proposed two options: a basic remote control with minimal functions (swapping channels, volume, and power) or a multifunctional remote that could control additional devices like a radio or a video recorder (VCR).

questions.question: What was the finding of the market?
questions.reference_answer: Marketing did a usability lab-test with a hundred people and found that users disliked the ugly look of current remote controls and the market segmentation includes different attitudes towards new functions. Users felt it hard to learn new functions and they zapped a lot. The channel switch was the most popular function while the power, volume and channel selections buttons were very relevant. The market was to be segmented to different groups and most users were between thirty-six and forty-five years old and young users had different tastes about the LCD compared to the old. The speech recognition features were welcomed by the second largest group, the young but which group they should targeted remained to be discussed. Marketing concluded that less important functions should be discarded and the device should be user friendly.

oracle.answer: The finding of the market was that the majority of users (60%) fall into the age group of 16 to 45 years, who are highly interested in new features and are more critical about their money spending. The second group, aged 46 to 65, is less interested in new features but spends money more easily. The usability and design of the remote control were key factors, with users finding current remote controls difficult to use and generally unattractive. Younger users were more open to new features like LCD displays and speech recognition compared to older users.

questions.question: What did the team discuss about the new features?
questions.reference_answer: Industrial Designer argued that the LCD and speech recognition features would largely add to cost. Project Manager said that the LCD would be cheaper than speech recognition and might be a good idea. The team would come back on that later.

oracle.answer: The team discussed that they wanted to include features appealing to younger people, such as LCD or speech recognition. However, the Industrial Designer noted that these features would be costly, exceeding their budget. The Marketing representative agreed, while the User Interface suggested that a 25 Euro remote was not affordable. The Project Manager proposed using LCD instead of speech recognition, which was cheaper and could be a viable option.

questions.question: What did the team say about the new product requirements?
questions.reference_answer: Project Manager decided that the remote control should only be used on television and targeted at the biggest size of group. Corporate colour and slogan must be used on the cover. They agreed that a power button, channel switches from zero to nine, volume control, mute should be contained and a small-size menu included.

oracle.answer:
The team discussed several new product requirements for the remote control, including:

- Power button
- Channel selection (zero to nine)
- Volume control
- Menu button
- Four arrow buttons for channel and volume selection (up-down for channels, left-right for volume)
- Option to display the menu on either the LCD screen or the remote control, with the preference being the remote control due to compatibility across different televisions

Marketing suggested that having a nice-looking remote control and keeping it simple would appeal to the younger market, potentially justifying higher costs. The mute function was considered but decided against as it would require more than one step to operate.
